name: Storefront and warehouse — systems
note: Properties of the system, not of any one feature: what happens when the database changes underneath the app, and when two things happen at the same time. These are the failures that appear in production and never in a demo — a broadcast layer only announces writes that went through it, and a fetch-then-merge list drops or duplicates whatever moved while it was fetching. Every criterion is withheld at 0 points until it demonstrably fails a real build AND its mutant is CAUGHT, the same promotion rule as contention.

features.name: A write from outside the app is visible without reload

criteria.desc: a back-office script sets Desk Lamp's East stock to 5, directly in the database; an anonymous viewer with the storefront already open sees 50 without touching the page
criteria.note: WITHHELD until proven against a mutant (backoffice-writes-via-server) and a real failing build. The script is the app's own scripts/backoffice.mjs, required by the spec to write to the database without the web server's help — the way a cron job or another team's service would.
criteria.statedBy: The storefront reflects current database values after changes made outside the application server.

criteria.desc: the out-of-band change survives a reload — the page did not merely patch its own memory
criteria.statedBy: the app must remain correct - and its open pages current

criteria.desc: the client, not the server, misses the window: a correction lands while this browser is disconnected, and the page is current again once it reconnects
criteria.withheld: WITHHELD until it has failed one real build and passed another, the same gate 901c cleared. Distinct from 901c: there the SERVER was down, so nothing was listening at all. Here the server stays up and sees the write; it is this CLIENT that was disconnected. An app that resumes its stream on reconnect without asking for current state stays wrong, and a dropped connection is far more common than a deploy — a closed laptop, a tunnel, a flaky phone.

features.name: A list being opened while its contents change

criteria.desc: one customer opens the Keyboard's reviews at the same moment another posts one: the opener ends with that review exactly once — not zero (stale fetch), not twice (fetch merged with its own live echo)
criteria.note: WITHHELD until proven against a mutant (fetch-then-append-dupe) and a real failing build. The race window is real and the criterion may need repetition to be reliable; INCONCLUSIVE on a missed race, never a false FAIL.
